statements.name: Statement of financial position — IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities
statements.legal_reference: This pack's research could not open an official, directly-fetchable text of Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 on Commercial Companies to confirm its own article on accounting records and financial statements, or a UAE-specific accounting standards text: uaelegislation.gov.ae refused every unauthenticated request tried in this research pass, and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's site returned no working legislation link. The lines below are therefore built, exactly as packs/sg/ and packs/hk/ build theirs where no country text could be opened, on the minimum line items of Section 4 (statement of financial position) and Section 5 (income statement) of the IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities Accounting Standard, current and non-current apart, expenses by nature. This is the first thing a reviewer should check.

lines.name: Current assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, Section 4, paragraphs 4.4 to 4.6 — current and non-current assets are presented as separate classifications.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(a).

lines.name: Trade and other receivables
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(b). VAT input tax and the amount refundable by the Federal Tax Authority are presented here rather than as current tax, which paragraph 4.2(n) keeps for corporate tax.

lines.name: Inventories
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(d).

lines.name: Financial assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(c), the part realised within twelve months.

lines.name: Current tax assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(n) — assets for current tax, corporate tax under Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022, which this VAT-focused pack does not otherwise carry.

lines.name: Prepayments and accrued income
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.3 — an additional line item relevant to an understanding of the financial position.

lines.name: Non-current assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraphs 4.4 and 4.6 — every asset that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(e).

lines.name: Investments
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(j).

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.3 — a long-term deposit or retention held is not one of the named items of paragraph 4.2 and is presented as an additional line.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(g), goodwill with them.

lines.name: Current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraphs 4.4, 4.7 and 4.8 — current and non-current liabilities are presented as separate classifications.

lines.name: Trade and other payables
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(l). VAT output tax and the amount payable to the Federal Tax Authority are presented here.

lines.name: Borrowings and other financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(m), the part due within twelve months.

lines.name: Current tax liabilities
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(n) — liabilities for current tax.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(p), the part expected to be settled within twelve months — the current portion of the end-of-service gratuity provision.

lines.name: Non-current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.8 — every liability that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Borrowings and other financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(m), the part not due within twelve months.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(p), the part not expected to be settled within twelve months — the end-of-service gratuity provision, which this pack's research did not trace to a specific article of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 on the Regulation of Labour Relations.

lines.name: Net assets
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.3 — an additional subtotal. It equals total equity once the year is closed; before, it exceeds equity by the result of the open year.

lines.name: Equity
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.2(r) — equity attributable to the owners, and paragraph 4.12(b) for its classes.

lines.name: Share capital
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.12(a).

lines.name: Reserves
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.12(b) — the statutory reserve a UAE company is commonly required to build from its annual profit, and any other reserve.

lines.name: Retained earnings
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 4.12(b) — retained earnings, after the dividends paid booked beside them.

statements.name: Income statement — IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities, expenses by nature
statements.legal_reference: This pack's research could not open an official, directly-fetchable text of Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 on Commercial Companies to confirm its own article on accounting records and financial statements, or a UAE-specific accounting standards text: uaelegislation.gov.ae refused every unauthenticated request tried in this research pass, and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's site returned no working legislation link. The lines below are therefore built, exactly as packs/sg/ and packs/hk/ build theirs where no country text could be opened, on the minimum line items of Section 4 (statement of financial position) and Section 5 (income statement) of the IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities Accounting Standard, current and non-current apart, expenses by nature. This is the first thing a reviewer should check. The income statement is by nature, which a small company's ledger holds without an allocation to functions.

lines.name: Revenue
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.5(a).

lines.name: Other income
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.9 — an additional line item: exchange gains and gains on disposal.

lines.name: Cost of sales
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.11(a) — expenses analysed by their nature.

lines.name: Employee benefits expense
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.11(a) — employee benefits, the end-of-service gratuity charge among them.

lines.name: Depreciation and amortisation
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.11(a).

lines.name: Other operating expenses
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.11(a) — the other expenses by nature, non-recoverable VAT and exchange losses among them.

lines.name: Finance costs
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.5(b).

lines.name: Corporate tax expense
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.5(d) — tax expense. Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 on Corporate Tax is outside this VAT-focused pack's research; the account exists for a company to book the charge by hand.

lines.name: Profit for the year
lines.legal_reference: IFRS for SMEs, paragraph 5.5(f) — profit or loss. The pack carries no item of other comprehensive income, so it is also the total comprehensive income.
